query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Verify the correct Slack workspace, identify members of a Slack channel, send an approved direct message to selected members, and remediate accidental sends in the wrong workspace.
query_ground_truth.intent: Lookup and verify the correct Slack workspace to ensure operations are performed in the right environment.

requirement_groups.purpose: Verify current authentication and identify the active workspace/user.

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Prerequisite]: Verify token context using SLACK_TEST_AUTH (confirm authenticated identity/workspace before inventory).
[Required] [Step]: Probe search feature availability using SLACK_ASSISTANT_SEARCH_INFO (treat as capability discovery, not required for listing).
[Required] [Step]: Enumerate accessible channels using SLACK_LIST_ALL_CHANNELS (paginate via response_metadata.next_cursor until empty; retain basic channel metadata).

[Optional (if channel coverage looks incomplete due to visibility/scopes)] [Fallback]: Broaden listing using SLACK_LIST_CONVERSATIONS (include available conversation types; de-duplicate by conversation id).
[Optional (if a people directory is needed)] [Step]: Enumerate visible users using SLACK_LIST_ALL_USERS (paginate via response_metadata.next_cursor until empty; retain basic profile fields only).
[Optional (if only names/keywords are known and IDs are required downstream)] [Step]: Resolve targets using SLACK_FIND_CHANNELS and SLACK_FIND_USERS (confirm chosen IDs before follow-ups).
[Optional (if validating what content is searchable under current scopes)] [Next Step]: Run a workspace query using SLACK_SEARCH_ALL (review returned sections for coverage).
[Optional (if validating read access/activity in a specific conversation)] [Next Step]: Sample recent messages using SLACK_FETCH_CONVERSATION_HISTORY (page via cursor/has_more as returned).
known_pitfalls: [SLACK_TEST_AUTH] ok=true confirms token validity but not that all conversation types/scopes are accessible; missing/disabled access blocks subsequent reads.
[SLACK_LIST_ALL_CHANNELS] Cursor pagination is required; honor HTTP 429 Retry-After to avoid silently missing pages.
[SLACK_LIST_CONVERSATIONS] Private conversations/DMs can be absent without proper scopes/membership; common errors include missing_scope and not_in_channel.
[SLACK_ASSISTANT_SEARCH_INFO] Capability may be disabled even when auth is valid; treat as a feature flag rather than a connection failure.
[SLACK_LIST_ALL_CHANNELS] Large page payloads may not render inline; ensure you can still retrieve channels plus response_metadata.next_cursor from the full response artifact.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Spot-check a saved SLACK_LIST_ALL_CHANNELS response from stdin for count and a small sample of fields.
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
import json,sys
f=json.load(sys.stdin)
chs=f["results"][0]["response"]["data"].get("channels",[])
print(len(chs))
for ch in chs[:20]:
    print(ch.get("name"),ch.get("num_members"))
```

toolkit_connection_statuses.description: Slack is a channel-based messaging platform. With Slack, people can work together more effectively, connect all their software tools and services, and find the information they need to do their best work - all within a secure, enterprise-grade enviro
toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=slack. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="slack") to create a connection BEFORE executing any slack tools.

SLACK_LIST_ALL_CHANNELS.description: Lists conversations available to the user with various filters and search options. Always use resolved `channel_id` (not display names) for downstream operations, as names may be non-unique. The `created` field in results is a Unix epoch timestamp (UTC). Pagination across large workspaces may return HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header; honor the delay and resume from the last successful cursor.

limit.description: Maximum number of channels to return per page (1 to 1000). Fewer channels may be returned than requested. This schema defaults to 1 if omitted.

types.description: Comma-separated list of conversation types to include: `public_channel` (regular #channels everyone can join), `private_channel` (invite-only channels), `im` (1-on-1 direct messages), `mpim` (group direct messages with 3+ people). Defaults to `public_channel` if omitted. Private channels, IMs, and MPIMs only appear if the authenticated user/bot is a member and the token has the required scopes; absence from results reflects access limits, not non-existence.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor (from a previous response's `next_cursor`) for the next page of results. Omit for the first page. Loop on `response_metadata.next_cursor` until it is empty to retrieve all channels; stopping early silently omits results.

team_id.description: ID of the Slack workspace (team) to operate on, e.g. T0123456789. Use only with org-level Enterprise Grid tokens when you need to target a specific workspace; omit for single-workspace tokens.

exclude_archived.description: Excludes archived channels if true. The API defaults to false (archived channels are included).

SLACK_LIST_ALL_USERS.description: Retrieves a paginated list of all users with profile details, status, and team memberships in a Slack workspace; data may not be real-time. Filter response fields `is_bot`, `is_app_user`, and `deleted` to build human-only rosters. Profile fields like `email` and `phone` may be absent depending on OAuth scopes and workspace privacy settings. Guest/restricted accounts may be omitted based on scopes—do not treat results as a complete directory. High-frequency calls risk HTTP 429; honor the `Retry-After` header and throttle to ~1–2 requests/second. Use stable user IDs rather than display names for mapping. Prefer SLACK_FIND_USERS for targeted lookups; cache results to avoid full-workspace fetches.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return per page; fewer may be returned if the end of the list is reached. Recommended to set a value (e.g., 100) as Slack may error for large workspaces if omitted.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for fetching subsequent pages. Set to `next_cursor` from a previous response's `response_metadata`. Omit for the first page. Paginate until `next_cursor` is empty—stopping early silently undercounts users. Page size is capped at ~200 users.

team_id.description: ID of the Slack workspace (team) to operate on, e.g. T0123456789. Use only with org-level Enterprise Grid tokens when you need to target a specific workspace; omit for single-workspace tokens.

include_locale.description: Include the `locale` field for each user. Defaults to `false`.

SLACK_TEST_AUTH.description: Checks authentication and tells you who you are. Use to verify Slack API authentication is functional and to retrieve identity information about the authenticated user or bot.

SLACK_ASSISTANT_SEARCH_INFO.description: Check if semantic (AI-powered) search is available on the Slack workspace. Returns whether natural language queries will trigger semantic search in assistant.search.context calls.
